extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH biographical sketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing NIH-format biographical sketches for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors, following the specified headings, ordering, and page limits used in NIH grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact format/ordering provided for each person and keep the entire biographical sketch to no more than four pages. This is an overriding formatting/length requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required header fields
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME; POSITION TITLE; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these header identifiers at the top of each person's biosketch so the reviewer can readily identify the individual and link to eRA Commons records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training entry
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable.) INSTITUTION AND LOCATION; DEGREE (if applicable) MM/YY; FIELD OF STUDY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List education/training in chronological order beginning with the baccalaureate. For each entry include institution and location, degree, month/year, and field of study. Include postdoctoral and residency training where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the individual's role on the proposed project and summarize qualifications and experience relevant to that role. Describe how past experience, expertise, leadership, training, and previous projects make the person well suited for their proposed responsibilities (examples in text: overseeing recruitment, sample acquisition, laboratory conduct, analysis, mentoring, leading multicenter trials, etc.). Make the statement project-specific and succinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Employment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological list of positions and employment (dates and titles). Include prior academic and professional appointments, administrative/committee positions, and relevant committee or leadership service. Also list Honors (awards, fellowships) under this heading or adjacent to positions as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: B (administrative/committee service) and Honors detail
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current and past administrative/committee roles (with dates) and honors/awards, as demonstrated (e.g., membership on boards, working groups, editorial boards). Include dates and concise role descriptions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a selected list of peer-reviewed publications relevant to the proposed work. Use chronological order if indicated (the example states 'Selected peer-reviewed publications relevant to this project (from over 140, in chronological order)'). Include citations sufficient for identification (authors, title, journal, year, volume/pages). Select publications most pertinent to the proposed project or role.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research Support (Ongoing and Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support — Ongoing Research Support; Completed Research Support (last 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List active and recently completed research support with sponsoring agency, grant number, PI name, project dates, project title, a brief statement of goals, and the individual's role (e.g., Principal Investigator, Co-Investigator, Project Manager, Scientist). Separate ongoing vs. completed support and include specific dates and concise project descriptions as shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role specification in Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: For each research support entry, specify the individual's role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Project Manager, Scientist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the role for each listed grant (the examples show 'Role: Principal Investigator', 'Role: Senior Scientist', 'Role: Project Manager, Scientist'). This clarifies responsibilities and level of involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project description for Research Support entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short goal/description for each listed grant (e.g., 'The goal of this project is to develop a low-cost, no amplification, nucleic acid diagnostic technology for respiratory pathogens.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each grant entry should include a concise statement of the project's aims/goals to convey relevance and scope; keep descriptions brief but specific enough to communicate the nature of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity and relevance of items
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and present items (personal statement content, publications, research support) that are particularly relevant to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examples emphasize choosing publications and describing experience that directly support the person's proposed contributions (e.g., assays, diagnostics, clinical trial leadership). Prioritize relevance over exhaustiveness within the four-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of publication and grant citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations for publications and research support should include standard bibliographic elements (authors, title, journal, year, volume/pages) and grant identifiers (agency and grant number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete and standard citation information so reviewers can readily locate the referenced work or grant; include identifiers such as PMCID when applicable (one example includes 'PMCID: 3529779').
